quests.title: The Count Does Not Add Up

steps.text: Nine wells on the west road are failing. Sura the well-rider drinks in the tavern.
Sura’s map says they are failing in ORDER. Hold it against Bahri’s count at the oasis.
The tally balances to the drop, and it is written in the bazaar. Find Qasim al-Warid’s stall.
The broker points at the Emir’s signature. Somebody at that end of the market watches every cart that goes west.
Three carts, west empty and back heavy, four months running. The quiet trade off the square deals in paper.
An unsigned manifest with an off-world berth on it. Ask Rafiq what the code means.
The way station, two legs west along the caravan road.
A siphon rig on the pipe head. The one in the plated coat is the only one out here who can start it again.
The pipe has stopped. Take it up the castle path.
The road is shut and Kufa was never told. You are carrying the Seal of the Waterway.
Read out at the well at sundown, by the fox who signed it. Kufa knows, and Kufa is digging.
Bashir’s crew have the cistern head open and drawing clean for the first time in fourteen months.
Ummi Reyhan’s nephew Dahab drove a cart west four months ago. Nobody at the castle will write his name down.
Alive at the way station. Tell Ummi Reyhan at the camel pen — and she will ask about the cart.
Dahab is walking home. The cart is fine.
Kufa’s reserve is under the stadium infield. Master Faruq runs the Watch on it.
Break three waves at the cistern head. Put the four drain mouths down as well for a second purse.
The draw is yours. The drain mouths are still open.
Three waves, every mouth down, and the crews voted you the purse.
Faruq keeps goal. There is a ball in the store and a spot on the grass.
You beat him from the spot on his own line. He has written it in the book.
Captain Idris wants the whole first leg of the caravan road cleared. Not thinned — cleared.
His runner walked the leg end to end and nothing came out of the shoulders at him.
Three wagons loaded and standing in the bazaar pen. The hiring board has been up five weeks.
Ghazi wants an escort to the way station on the far leg. Two legs of road.
West out of the market. The wagons roll when the road ahead of them is clear.
First leg done. The far leg is the one that ate the last two caravans.
All three at the station. Ghazi is at the board in the bazaar.
Paid in full, and the board is yours whenever you want a road walked.
Ghazi hired one extra sword for a load of dry goods. His name is Kass.
The far leg was waiting for this run. They walked through the wagons, not at them.
Kass is cut badly, still on his feet, and will not go anywhere but the oasis. Ask the fox on the dock about his boat.
The wagons are on the way station forecourt and Rukaya has written the entry.
Ghazi’s board is open to you. Ask what is on it.
THE CISTERN TRAIN — Four wagons to the way station and back. Both legs.
THE CISTERN TRAIN is through. Ghazi is at the board in the bazaar.
Paid for the cistern train.
THE PIPE-HEAD SWEEP — Clear the far leg so Idris’s repair crew can work. No wagons.
THE PIPE-HEAD SWEEP is through. Ghazi is at the board in the bazaar.
Paid for the pipe-head sweep.
THE MILESTONE RUN — Two wagons of grain to the milestone. First leg only.
THE MILESTONE RUN is through. Ghazi is at the board in the bazaar.
Paid for the milestone run.
THE WESTWARD TRAIN — Six wagons of water going west. Both legs, in daylight.
THE WESTWARD TRAIN is through. Ghazi is at the board in the bazaar.
Paid for the westward train.
Every contract on the board walked, and the last of them carried water west out of Kufa in daylight.
There is a boat on a pond with no fish in it, and Bahri sits in it.
Kass walked the far leg with you and was cut on it. He is still walking, and he will not go anywhere but the oasis.
Bahri says take the boat to the middle of the water and stop there. No questions.
Station 9 is under the oasis. The arch would not read his face and the corridor is awake.
Five station frames in Operations, between you and anyone who can help him.
They have carried him through the ward door. It is not locked.
He is on the table under the lamp, and awake enough to argue.
They want the crystal to sell. Kass will not give it to them.
Kass gave you the crystal and stayed behind to build something out of the four who will listen.

quests.title: The One in the Plated Coat

steps.text: The berth code is for a cut field north of the way station. There is a lander on it in a red band.
More goes up the gantry than comes in on the carts. Nuri raised it twice and was visited once.
His guard is on the field, in the same brown as the frames at the choke.
He is on the ramp and he is not running.
Six thousand, the berth and four years of signed sheets, for the crystal.
You said no. He is the last thing standing on this field.
He said it in front of Rukaya and she wrote it down. Kufa has a name.
Nobody on Kufa will ever know who he was. You have the sheet, and the sheet has nine more places on it.
Kass has taken a store room off Operations and carried lamps into it.
Sahar on signals, Tal in stores, Ammar from the ward — and Diya, who is not there yet.
Three of the eleven went up the shaft with the station’s bearings. Ask Rukaya at the way station.
"Three, unnamed, west." She has them, at an hour when nobody walks.
They walked into a yard that now owns the pad. Rukaya has them and does not want them.
They reached a closed pad and went into the desert. The shipping sheet says where they will surface.
The ship took them, and the bearings and the corridor plans with them.
Bahri has been the resistance for nine years and is not coming to any meetings.
Four in a cancelled store room under carried lamps. Nobody voted.
Rafiq does not want anything off his shelves moved. He wants things out of pockets and he knows whose.
NIGHT EYES — four sessions with somebody he knows. They have to be a third closer before they notice you.
Ghazi’s loading bill, at the camel pen.
A second line in another hand, unsigned. Ghazi never knew what was on his own train.
Master Faruq’s Watch roster, under the stadium.
Nine nights with nobody on the head, every one signed off as a full watch.
Qasim al-Warid’s brass seal ring. He never takes it off.
There is no broker — there is one office and a stall it put in the market. Rafiq paid in GHOST STEP.
The Seal of the Waterway, on the Emir’s person.
Off the Emir, out of his own throne room. Rafiq is shutting for a month.
And his own slip says he sells to all of them and has never told any of them about the others.
The crystal is cold in your pack and nobody on Kufa is to know you are carrying it. The transport pad is on the town square.
He was already standing on it, and he did not come alone. Ghazi, Sahar and Rafiq came in with you.
He has broken off and backed to the north edge. He is leaving, and he wants to say it to your face first.
The pad is clear. There are nine more places on his run that have never heard of you.

note: THE FIRST LEG
Two legs west. The way station is at the far end of the second.
THE SIPHON
A rig the size of a house, and the pipe under it goes down further than the well in the square. It is not taking the wells. It is taking what is under them.
THE PIPE STOPS
It takes about a minute to wind down and it is the loudest minute on the road. Kufa does not know yet.
SUNDOWN
Bahri reads for forty minutes and nobody leaves. The Emir stands the whole time. At the end of it somebody at the back asks where the shovels are kept, and that is the moment the town survives.
THE GATE, THIS MORNING
Two crews being paid off and neither of them told why. One of them is arguing about the season. The season is going to get the blame for a long time.
THE CISTERN HEAD
The ring in the middle of the infield is the top of Kufa’s reserve. Four drain mouths run out to the west road, and the west road is low.
THE DRAW IS YOURS
Three waves and the cistern head still standing. Faruq is at the tunnel mouth.
THE CREWS’ PURSE
Every mouth on the infield put down. Faruq said they would vote for it and they voted for it.
CARAVAN — HIRING
Three wagons loaded and standing in the pen. The board has been up five weeks.
THEY ARE BEHIND YOU
The wagons roll while the road ahead is clear and stop the moment it is not. Get in front of them.
FIRST LEG
The wagons are through to the far leg. Nobody has done the first leg in a year.
THE WAY STATION
Three wagons on the forecourt and the crews walking. Ghazi is at the board in the bazaar.
THEY GOT IN AMONG THE WAGONS
Walk back out to the bazaar and Ghazi will hitch the spare set. He will not enjoy it.
THEY GOT IN AMONG THE WAGONS
Leave the road and come back, and the far leg starts again.
FIRST LEG
Through the milestone. The far leg starts west of here.
AT THE STATION
All of it through. Ghazi is at the board in the bazaar.
THE CONTRACT IS LOST
Ghazi will want telling, and he will put it back on the board.
THE CONTRACT IS LOST
Ghazi will want telling, and he will put it back on the board.
THE FAR LEG IS QUIET
Nothing standing between the milestone and the station. Tell Ghazi.
AT THE MILESTONE
The wagons are in. Ghazi is at the board.
FIRST LEG
Through the milestone. The far leg starts west of here.
AT THE STATION
All of it through. Ghazi is at the board in the bazaar.
THE CONTRACT IS LOST
Ghazi will want telling, and he will put it back on the board.
THE CONTRACT IS LOST
Ghazi will want telling, and he will put it back on the board.
THE WATER OPENS
Not a hatch and not a jetty — nothing you could have seen from the shore. The skiff is taken hold of from underneath.
THE ARCH
It reads a face by its edges and half of his are four days old. The lights go along the hall the wrong colour, one after another.
KASS, AT YOUR SHOULDER
“Mines in the floor and lines across it. Walk it like you are reading it. They are not for you. They are for the day somebody finds us, and today that is you.”
OPERATIONS
Five of them, and they are already up.
THAT IS NOT THE ROAD
Nothing that lives out here is made of plate. They came to the choke and waited, and they let the first four wagons of the week go past.
THE WAY STATION
A wall, a gate, a well and the head of the cistern the whole road exists to reach. Both legs were coming here.
THE BERTH
A cut field, a gantry and a lander in a red band. This is where the surplus went, and the berth code you are carrying is for this pad.
PLATE ON THE FIELD
The same plate, in the same brown, as the frames that came out of the alcoves at the choke. Nobody ever said whose they were.
THE PAD IS QUIET
The lander is grounded and the cutters are still running, because nobody ever turns the cutters off.
THE OLD WING
A store room signed out to a project that was cancelled in the station’s first year. Somebody has carried lamps into it.
THE FOUR WHO WILL LISTEN
Sahar, Tal, Ammar and Diya, in a store room signed out to a cancelled project, under lamps somebody carried in. Nobody voted. Nobody is going to.
THE ROAD TO THE STANDS
Something has been at the gate, and not for a day or two. Nobody has come out to look, which tells you how long.
THE GATE IS CLEAR
For now. Nothing about the reason they came has changed, and the stone is scored to the depth of a hand where they were working at it.

npcs.name: Hadi

topics.label: Anything for a long walk west?
replies: Two legs of road and no shade worth the name on either.
I have put a filled canteen on the shelf for you. Honest weight, and I have not marked it up, which you may take as a comment on how seriously I take the west road.

topics.label: And this month?
replies: Down. First time in four years it has gone the other way.
Not far. Not enough that anybody has said thank you. But I have re-chalked the board and I did not have to be embarrassed doing it.
You will not get a fuss out of this town. You will get a slightly shorter queue, which is the same thing said quietly.

topics.label: And now the head is open?
replies: Two thirds of what it was in the spring. I have started stocking things I stopped stocking.
A house with water spare buys soap, and cloth, and a thing for a child. Four years I have sold water and rope and nothing else and I had forgotten what this shop is for.
Everything on that shelf is cheaper to you from now on and I am not going to explain why to anybody who asks.

note: TWO THIRDS OF THE SPRING PRICE
Hadi has started stocking things he stopped stocking.

topics.label: Who is actually buying, at those prices?
replies: Everybody, which is what makes it a good trade and a bad answer.
What I can tell you is who is NOT. The castle has not bought a drop from this market in four years, and the castle has eleven households in it.
A place that has stopped needing to buy has either found some or stopped drinking, and I have met the Emir’s steward and he is not thirsty.

note: THE CASTLE HAS NOT BOUGHT A DROP
Four years, eleven households, nothing through the market.

topics.label: What is a house paying for water this month?
replies: More than last month, less than next. Same as everything.
I quote three prices and I mean the second one. That one has gone up twice since the turn of the season and I have not enjoyed either.

npcs.greeting: Come in out of the sun. Everything here is honest weight.
npcs.bio: Keeps the shop off the square. Will quote you three prices and mean the second one.

npcs.name: Zohra

topics.label: I have to take something apart out on the road.
replies: Apart. Not open — apart.
Then not a blade. A blade is for a thing with a neck. Take the maul off the rack; I have put it out.
And do not pay me the first price. I would be embarrassed.

note: THE ARMORY
Zohra has put the maul on the counter.

topics.label: The town owes you one.
replies: The town owes YOU one and the town is famously bad at that, so I am doing it for them.
The spear and the claws are on the rack and they are on the rack at cost. Do not argue in my forge.

topics.label: There is plate out on that road.
replies: Plate. You are certain. Not banded, not scaled — plate.
Then somebody rolled it, and nobody on this planet can roll. We forge and we band, because we have a wood shortage and a coal shortage and a hundred and ten years of doing it that way.
Whatever came out of those alcoves at you was made somewhere with a mill, and a mill is a thing you can see from orbit.
I have been shoeing camels for thirty years and that is the most interesting sentence anybody has said in this room.

note: SOMEBODY WITH A MILL
Nobody on Kufa can roll plate. Whatever hit the caravan was made somewhere with a mill.

topics.label: His axe. You have had it on your bench.
replies: Twice. He brought it in the week before the run and he stood there while I did it, which nobody does.
It is not a caravan guard’s axe. The haft is short for a wagon and long for a corridor, and it is weighted to be swung indoors by somebody who has been taught to.
I said none of that to him and I am not going to say it to anybody else. He paid, he was civil, and a smith who talks about what is on her bench has an empty bench.

note: NOT A CARAVAN GUARD’S AXE
Short haft for a wagon, long for a corridor, weighted to be swung indoors. Zohra sharpened it twice and said nothing.

topics.label: The Warden was a boiler on three legs.
replies: It was OURS. That is the part nobody wants from me.
Brass, banded, riveted the way my grandmother riveted — a Kufan frame, built here, in the old yard, before anybody thought to write down who for.
Somebody bought a piece of this town’s own work and pointed it at the town’s own water. I would like that on a wall somewhere.

note: THE WARDEN WAS OURS
Brass, banded, riveted in the old yard. A Kufan frame, bought and pointed at Kufa’s own water.

topics.label: I brought you a piece of the KASPER plate.
replies: Sit down. No — stand there and do not touch anything.
It is one piece. Rolled, folded, rolled again, and there is no weld anywhere in it. I could put my whole shop on this and get an edge that would not hold a candle to it.

I am going to spend six months on this and produce something worse, and then six more, and eventually I will produce something better, because that is how it works and nobody in a hurry has ever understood that.
Four hundred. Do not argue — I would have paid eight and you would have taken two.

note: ROLLED, FOLDED, ROLLED AGAIN
No weld anywhere in it. Zohra has six months of work and then six more, and then something better.

topics.label: Brass over steel — why?
replies: Steel cooks you. You stand in that sun in a steel plate and you are a pot.
Brass is soft and it is honest about being soft. Everything in Kufa is one or the other.

npcs.greeting: Brass over steel out here. Steel cooks you.
npcs.bio: Beats brass and steel in the armory. Works in the heat by choice and thinks the rest of the town is soft.

npcs.name: Nasrin

topics.label: What is the table in the corner?
replies: Eight rods, twenty-two little men and a ball that has been in this room longer than I have.
A crew left it against a bill nine years ago and said they would come back and settle. They did not. So it is mine, and it has earned better than they ever did.
Slide the rods, hit the ball, five goals wins. Everybody in this town thinks they are good at it.

note: THE TABLE IN THE CORNER
Nasrin keeps a foosball table by the wall. First to five.

topics.label: About that game on the table.
replies: You beat it. Not me — the table. Nobody beats me.
Come back when the road is open and we will find out.

topics.label: The standpipe at the gate is down to a trickle.
replies: Down since the turn of the season, and we are only halfway through it.

It is not the square you want, though. It is the west road. Nine wells out there and they are going one after another — I get that off every crew that comes through this door, and I get it a full day before the castle does.
Sura rides those wells. She counts them. She is sat over there and she has been quiet for a week, which is not like her at all.

note: THE WEST ROAD
Nine wells failing. Sura the well-rider is in this room.

topics.label: Anything else worth hearing?
replies: Only that the broker’s runner drinks in here now and pays in coin nobody else out here is carrying.
I do not ask. What a man’s money looks like is not my business until he stops spending it.

topics.label: The road is open.
replies: Two crews in here last night arguing about who gets the next load. Arguing. Over the west road.
I have not heard that argument in a year and a half. Sit down.

topics.label: It is done.
replies: I heard before you got through the door. That is the entire trade.
Sit down. This one is free, and you can tell me the parts I have got wrong.

topics.label: What is the board saying?
replies: That Ghazi is hiring and that only fools are taking it, which around here is a recommendation.
Two trains gone on the far leg in a season. He has stood at that pen every morning since with a sheet nobody will put a name on.
Go and put a name on it. He will be rude to you and he will mean it kindly.

topics.label: Anybody talking about the stadium?
replies: Only the crews, and only in here, and only after the second one.
There is a reserve under that infield that this town does not think about because thinking about it means admitting it is the last of it.
Master Faruq comes in on a Thursday and has one and goes home. Eleven years. Never says a word about the job and never once been late.

topics.label: Who sits in a boat on a pond with no fish?
replies: Ha. You have met Bahri.

Nine years he has sat in that thing. My mother asked him once and he said he liked to sit in it, and she said that is not an answer, and he said no it is not, and they were friends for thirty years after that.
Nobody on this planet has ever got a second sentence out of him about that boat. If you do, come back and tell me and the drink is on the house.

topics.label: They have a name for him now.
replies: They do, and they are saying it wrong, and by Thursday it will be a song.
Eleven years there has been a fox in a plated coat and no name, and everybody in this room had a story about him and not one of them had a name.
A town can carry almost anything if it is allowed to say what it is called. I did not know that until this week.

topics.label: Nobody seems to know why the pad shut.
replies: No. And it will be the weather by spring, and a bad season by the year after, and in ten years it will not have happened.
I am not complaining. My grandfather’s tavern burned down in a thing that never happened either and he lived a long life.
Somebody knows. Somebody always knows and comes in here and does not say. I have got very good at not looking at them.

npcs.greeting: Sit anywhere. Water is free, the rest is not.
npcs.bio: Runs the tavern by the gate. Hears every caravan rumour a day before the castle does.

npcs.name: Rafiq

topics.label: Three carts. West empty, back heavy.
replies: You have been talking to the camel woman. Everybody underestimates her. I never have.
I hold the way-station manifest. Unsigned — which is the interesting part, because a manifest nobody has signed is a manifest nobody will admit to, and somebody paid a great deal to keep it that way.
One hundred and eighty. I am not haggling and neither are you.

note: THE MANIFEST
A destination on the far leg, and a berth code that is not on this planet.

topics.label: Three carts. West empty, back heavy.
replies: You have been talking to the camel woman. Everybody underestimates her. I never have.
I hold the way-station manifest. Unsigned — which is the interesting part.
It costs one hundred and eighty. It costs YOU nothing, because I was in the stands the day you stood the Watch, and this shop pays what it owes even when nobody can see it do it.

note: THE MANIFEST
A destination on the far leg, and a berth code that is not on this planet.

topics.label: The code at the bottom of it.
replies: A berth number. Berths are off-world.

That is as far as I will go and it is further than I have ever gone for anybody. Whoever is buying is not on this planet, which means whoever is SELLING has been paid in something that does not spend here — and that is why the coin his runner puts on Nasrin’s bar looks wrong.
The destination on the paper is a way station on the far leg of the caravan road. Two legs west. Go in daylight.

note: THE FAR LEG
The way station at the end of the second leg of the caravan road.

topics.label: You said ask about nothing I see.
replies: I did. What I did not say is that there is nothing on those shelves worth asking about.
The trade is not the shelves. The trade is that there are eleven or twelve foxes on this planet carrying a piece of paper that would finish somebody, and none of them know it, and I know all of them.
You walk about. Nobody looks twice at you. That is a thing I cannot buy and have wanted for four years.
Come back when you want to hear what is in whose coat.

note: THE QUIET TRADE
Rafiq does not want anything off his shelves moved. He wants things out of pockets, and he knows exactly whose.

topics.label: The dark-adaption course. Six fifty.
replies: One thing. It is behind the counter and it is six hundred and fifty.
A dark-adaption course. Four sessions, and afterwards a fox has to be a third closer to you before he notices you are there at all.
It is not a trick and it is not a drug. It is that nobody has ever taught you to use your own eyes and I know somebody who teaches it.
Six fifty. It will make everything I am about to ask you for easier and I would rather you bought it first, which is the most honest sentence I have said this year.

note: NIGHT EYES
Four sessions with somebody Rafiq knows. Enemies must be a third closer before they notice you at all.

topics.label: The thing behind the counter.
replies: Six hundred and fifty, and I do not do credit.
Not because I distrust you. Because the fox who teaches it does not, and I am not subsidising your education out of my own pocket.

topics.label: Whose coat, then?
replies: Ghazi. The caravan master, at the pen, forty paces from where you are standing.
He carries a loading bill for every train he has ever put on that road. What went on the wagons, in his own hand, before anybody decided what the story was going to be.
I want the one from the run that got hit at the choke. Not a copy. His.
Two hundred when you have it. And do not fight him — he is sixty and he has been decent to you.

note: MARK: GHAZI
The loading bill, at the camel pen in the bazaar. What actually went on the wagons. Steal it — do not fight him.

topics.label: The loading bill.
replies: Dry goods, it says. In his hand, on the morning, before anybody had a reason to lie.
And underneath, in a different hand, a second line that is not dry goods and is not signed.
Somebody put a load on that train that Ghazi did not put there and did not know about. That is why the choke happened and Ghazi will go to his grave thinking it was his fault.
Two hundred. Do not tell him. I mean that as a kindness and I am aware of how it sounds.

note: THE SECOND LINE
Ghazi wrote "dry goods". Underneath, in another hand and unsigned, is a line that is not dry goods. He never knew.

topics.label: Who else.
replies: Master Faruq. Under the stadium, running the Cistern Watch, and the straightest fox on this planet.
He keeps a roster. Who stood which watch on which night, four months of it, and every night the draw dropped has a name against it.
He will not give it to me and he will not give it to you, and he is right not to, because it reads like an accusation and none of those crews did anything.
Two hundred and fifty. I want to be able to say which nights had nobody on them at all.

note: MARK: FARUQ
The Watch roster, under the stadium. Four months of who stood which night. He will not hand it over and he is right not to.

topics.label: The Watch roster.
replies: Nine nights with nobody on the head. Nine. In four months.

And every one of them signed off by the Emir’s office as a full watch, which means somebody up the path was writing down a thing they knew was not true and Faruq has been carrying the paper that proves it in his own coat.

He would have handed it over if I had told him what it said. I did not tell him because then he would have gone up that path himself and been very brave about it and that is how straight foxes get finished.
Two hundred and fifty.

note: NINE EMPTY NIGHTS
Nine nights in four months with nobody on the cistern head — and every one signed off by the Emir’s office as a full watch.

topics.label: And the third.
replies: Qasim al-Warid. You know him. You have bought from him and so have I.
He wears a brass seal ring. Every slip that has come out of that stall in eleven years has been pressed with it, including the one I sold you.
I would like to stop needing him. That is the entire reason and I am not going to dress it up.
Three hundred, and it is the hardest of the three because he never takes it off and he is not stupid.

note: MARK: QASIM
The brass seal ring, at the broker’s stall in the bazaar. He never takes it off.

topics.label: The seal ring.
replies: Ha.
Three hundred, and I am going to tell you the thing I was not going to tell you, because you took a ring off a fox’s hand in a crowded market and I did not think you would.

The press on this is not Qasim’s. It is the office’s. He has been signing the Emir’s paper with the Emir’s die for eleven years and calling himself a broker, and everybody in that market including me has been saying "the broker" and meaning a man who sells things.
There is no broker. There is one office and a stall it put in the market.

note: THERE IS NO BROKER
The die on Qasim’s ring is the Emir’s office. Eleven years of "the broker" was one office and a stall it put in the market.

topics.label: There is a fourth, is there not.
replies: There is, and I have been not saying it for a fortnight.
Emir Tahir carries the Seal of the Waterway on his person. Not the die — the Seal. The thing that says who may take water out of this ground.
He read the whole thing out at the well at sundown and then put it back in his coat, which I found remarkable and nobody else seems to have noticed.
Six hundred. It is eighty per cent that he catches you and he is in a room with a door and guards on the path, and I would think very carefully.

note: MARK: THE EMIR
The Seal of the Waterway, on his person, in the throne room. Eight times in ten he catches you.

topics.label: The Seal of the Waterway.
replies: You are not going to tell me how, and I am not going to ask, and I would like that on the record as the most restraint I have ever shown.
Six hundred.

And I am shutting for a month. Not because of you. Because a fox who can take that off that man is a fox somebody will eventually ask about, and I would rather not be behind this counter when they do.

note: THE SEAL OF THE WATERWAY
Off the Emir’s person, out of his own throne room. Rafiq is shutting for a month.

topics.label: I read your slip.
replies: You did. When?
Well. Then you know I sell to the plated coat, and to the office, and to two foxes at the way station and one under a pond, and that I have never once told any of them about any of the others.

I am not anybody’s. That is not a defence and I am not offering it as one — it is just the fact, and the fact is worse than being somebody’s, because a fox who is somebody’s at least stops when they stop.
Keep the slip. I have it memorised and you have earned an honest afternoon.

note: THE CODED SLIP
Everyone Rafiq sells to. The plated coat, the Emir’s office, two at the way station and one under a pond — and none of them has ever been told about the others.

topics.label: Nothing I can ask about.
replies: Correct. Good.

npcs.greeting: Look at what you like. Ask about nothing you see.
npcs.bio: Sells things the market will not. Never says who he sells them to, which is the entire service.

npcs.name: Emir Tahir

lines.text: Emir.
You walked in off the road, so you already know the first thing about Kufa.
Water is the law here. Everything else is negotiable.

topics.label: The wells on the west road.
replies: Sura’s map.
I have seen it. I have seen a version of it every month for four.
You will notice I am not asking you what you think it means. Go and find out what it means and then ask me your real question. I will answer that one.

topics.label: Water is the law here.
replies: And the law is thirsty. Yes. Everyone gets there eventually.

topics.label: Emir.
replies: Walk safely. Both roads.

npcs.bio: Holds Kufa, and the water rights, which out here are the same thing.

npcs.name: Captain Idris

lines.text: Captain.
The road west is not dangerous because of what lives there. It is dangerous because it is long.
Anything can beat you if it has enough hours to do it in.

topics.label: The two caravans you lost.
replies: Both on the first leg, both in daylight, both within a mile of the milestone.
I do not need heroes out there. I need the first leg to be BORING. A road that is boring is a road that crews will use, and a road that crews use is a road that stays open.
Clear it. Everything between the bazaar mouth and the far bend. There is a purse for it and I do not have to ask anybody for permission to hand it over.

note: THE FIRST LEG
Captain Idris wants the first leg of the caravan road cleared — all of it.

topics.label: The first leg is clear.
replies: I had the runner in an hour ago. He walked it. He walked the whole leg and nothing came out of the shoulders at him and he did not know what to do with himself.
Take it. And take this seriously, because I mean it as more than thanks: you are the first person to make that road boring in two years.

note: THE FIRST LEG IS OPEN
Captain Idris paid out of the barracks purse.

topics.label: It was a rig. Out at the way station.
replies: A RIG.
Four months I have been writing "hostile action, cause unknown" at the bottom of a form about the far leg.
Give me the bearing. I will have a crew standing on it by the day after tomorrow and they will take it apart down to the bolts, and then I am going to walk that form up the castle path myself.

topics.label: Ghazi’s wagons went through.
replies: I know. I had it off the way station before I had it off Ghazi.
Two caravans I lost, and I wrote hostile action, cause unknown, at the bottom of both. You have just made both of those forms wrong, and I am delighted about it.

topics.label: There is plate on that road.
replies: Say that again slowly.
I have written "bandits" on eleven reports in four years because bandits is a word the castle accepts and "I do not know" is not.
Plate is not bandits. Plate is somebody with a supply line, and a supply line has an end, and an end is a thing a soldier can go and stand on.
I cannot act on your word alone. Bring me an end and I will go and stand on it.

topics.label: The field north of the way station.
replies: A freight pad. On my planet. Two legs west of a road I have been losing caravans on.
And it is on a chart in the castle, signed, permitted, and entirely legal, which is why nobody has ever had to hide it from me.
That is the lesson and it is not one I enjoy. Nothing anybody did to Kufa in four years was illegal. Every single piece of it went through an office.

note: NOTHING ANYBODY DID WAS ILLEGAL
The pad is on a chart in the castle — signed, permitted, and never once hidden from the man who lost the caravans.

topics.label: Nine nights with nobody on the cistern head.
replies: Nine.

And signed off as full watches. By the office. Which means somebody wrote a muster that did not happen and somebody countersigned it and neither of them was Faruq, because Faruq keeps the paper that proves it and has been carrying it about in his own coat like a man with a stone in his shoe.
I am going up that path. Not tonight — I am not a fool — but I am going, and I am going to make somebody say it in a room with a door open.
You did not have to bring me this. I want you to know I am aware of that, and that whoever had it before you decided I was better off not knowing.
They were probably right. Bring me things anyway.

do.call: HE IS GOING UP THE PATH

note: HE IS GOING UP THE PATH
"You did not have to bring me this. Whoever had it before you decided I was better off not knowing. They were probably right. Bring me things anyway."

topics.label: The guard who would not give a name.
replies: I know the type and I have had four of them under me.
A fox who walks a mined corridor with a third of himself missing is not brave. Brave is a thing you do once. That is TRAINED, and somebody spent years and a great deal of money doing it to him.
I did not ask and I am not going to. He stood in front of Ghazi’s wagons and that is the whole of what I need to know about anybody.

topics.label: Captain.
replies: Water and shade. Off you go.

npcs.bio: Runs the barracks. Has lost two caravans and talks about both.

npcs.name: Sura

lines.text: You ride the wells?
Somebody has to count them. A well nobody visits is a well nobody digs out, and then it is sand.
Nine on the west road. Seven of them still give. Ask me again after the season.
Is the caravan road as bad as they say?
Worse in the middle, quiet at both ends. The wraiths out there are patient, not clever.
Keep moving and keep drinking. That is the whole of it.

topics.label: Nasrin says the west wells are going.
replies: Nine on the west road. Seven still give. I have said that to every fox in this room and it is true and it is not the answer.
Here is the answer. It was seven last season as well. It is not the SAME seven.
They are failing in ORDER. East to west, one every few days, straight down the line of the road like somebody walking it.
A season does not do that. A season takes the shallow ones and leaves the deep ones and it has no opinion at all about what order they stand in.
Take the map — I have put the dates on it. Then go and hold it up next to Bahri’s count at the oasis, because if I am right then his numbers cannot be.

note: SURA’S WELL MAP
Nine wells, dated. Bahri keeps the count at the oasis, south of the square.

topics.label: What am I looking for in his count?
replies: A month where the drawn matches the allowed. That is the whole thing.

Nobody draws to the drop. There is always a crew that took more than it was given and a crew that never turned up at all. A tally that balances has not been kept, it has been COPIED — one column written out of the other.

topics.label: You have been quiet about this.
replies: I am the well-rider. If I say the road is dying, the road is dying — that is not an opinion when I say it, it is a notice.
So I would like to be right first. You are the part where I find out.

topics.label: It is broken.
replies: I know. I rode out at first light and the eighth was wet at the bottom.
Go up the path. He will already know too, and he has known longer than either of us.

topics.label: Nothing for now.
replies: Then drink something. It is free in here and that is not true anywhere else in town.

npcs.bio: Kufa's well-rider. Has drawn every water map anybody trusts, and will not sell you the one she is still checking.

npcs.name: Bahri

lines.text: You guard the water?
I keep the count. Who drew, how much, and whether they left the shore as they found it.
The Emir writes the law in the hall. Out here I am the one who reads it aloud.
Would Kufa stand with us in a fight?
Kufa stands with whoever keeps the road open. Close it and we are nobody's ally.
Bring me a reason and I will bring the shore.

topics.label: Your count, next to her map.
replies: Show me.
The drawn matches the allowed. To the drop. Every month on this sheet, four months back.
I did not write those. I keep the SHORE tally — who came down, what they took off my water, whether they left the reeds standing. The allocation comes to me finished and I file it.
It comes from the bazaar. Qasim al-Warid’s stall. His runner brings it on the first of the month, and until this exact second I have never once thought about that.

note: THE TALLY BALANCES
The allocation is written in the bazaar, at the broker’s stall.

topics.label: Would you say this out loud?
replies: To the Emir? He signs those sheets. That is the difficulty and you worked it out before I finished the sentence.
Bring me something I can hold. Not a suspicion — out here a suspicion is weather. A paper with a destination on it.

topics.label: It is broken.
replies: Then the count starts meaning something again.
I am going to redo the year. All of it, from the shore up. It will take me a month and I have never wanted a month of work so badly.

topics.label: Keep the water.
replies: That is the job. Walk safely.

topics.label: Why is there a boat on a pond with no fish in it?
replies: I like to sit in it.
It just sits right there all the time. And sometimes I sit in it.

topics.label: Nobody rows a pond this size.
replies: No. They walk round it.
That is the whole trouble with the boat, and I have made my peace with it.

topics.label: I have one of yours. He is cut badly and he will not stop saying nine.
replies: Put him down. Gently. And do not ever put him down gently where anyone else can see you do it.
You are going to take the boat. Out to the middle of the water, and you are going to stop there.
No questions. Not one, not now. If you ask me anything at all standing on this shore I will have to answer it, and then I will have to explain to somebody why I answered it.
The count I keep is not only water. Go.

note: THE MIDDLE OF THE WATER
He told you to take the boat without once looking at it.

topics.label: About your boat.
replies: It just sits right there all the time.
And sometimes I sit in it.
Kass says you did not take anything you were not given. I have written that on the shore post, which is the only place I write anything, and it will still be there in ten years.

topics.label: Kass wants to know what you think.
replies: He does, does he. After nine years.
I will tell you what I told nobody, because nobody asked. There is one way in and out of that station and I have sat on it since I was thirty-four.
In nine years I have turned back two surveyors, a lost child and a man from the Emir’s office who did not know what he had found, and I did it with a story about liking to sit in a boat.
That IS the resistance. It has been the resistance the whole time. They have just got round to giving it a name and a room.
Tell him yes. Tell him I have been in since before he could shave, and tell him I am not coming to any meetings.

note: THE DOORMAN
"That IS the resistance. It has been the whole time. They have just got round to giving it a name and a room."

npcs.bio: Keeps the oasis. Two caravans owe him their whole crew and he has never once mentioned it to either of them.

npcs.name: Qasim al-Warid

lines.text: You are the broker.
I am the reason the crew behind you knows which well it draws from on Thursday.
Nobody thanks a man for that. They thank the well.

topics.label: You write Kufa’s water allocation.
replies: I broker it. Writing it down is the small part of it.
Somebody has to say which crew draws first when there are four crews and one well. If I did not, the answer out here would be whichever crew is biggest — and that is a worse law than mine.
You are holding Sura’s map. Everybody is holding Sura’s map; she gives it to anyone who asks and she asks nothing for it, which is the most expensive habit in this town.
Take your complaint up the castle path. He will show you his own signature at the bottom of every sheet you are angry about.

topics.label: Three carts go west empty and come back heavy.
replies: Carts go west empty. That is what west is FOR.
Ummi Reyhan should count her camels and leave my drivers alone. Half of them are her relatives.

note: HE DID NOT ANSWER IT
And he answered everything else in one breath.

topics.label: What is at the way station?
replies: Shade. A cistern. A door that locks.
Whatever else you think is out there, you are going to have to go and look at it, and I am not going to talk you out of the walk.

topics.label: Nothing. Carry on.
replies: I intend to.

npcs.bio: Licensed to write Kufa’s allocation. Stands under the hiring board because that is where the crews are, and the crews are the only people who ever read a sheet he has signed.

npcs.name: Ummi Reyhan

lines.text: You have the quiet end of the market.
It is a dead end, which means everything that comes down here has to come back past me. I have never had to go looking for news in my life.

topics.label: The broker’s carts.
replies: Three of them. West empty, back a month later riding so low the axles sing.
Four months of that. I have it on the stick.

There is nothing on that road to come back HEAVY with. So either he has found a way to sell sand at a profit, or what is in those carts went out west in the first place and is only pretending to come home.
My sister’s boy Dahab drove the third one out. He has not come back. Nobody at the castle will even write his name down — a driver is not a crew, they say, a driver is a cart.

note: THE THIRD CARAVAN
Dahab drove a cart west four months ago and did not come back.

topics.label: I found Dahab. He is alive.
replies: Say the second part again.
Alive. At the station. Hauling for the thing that was killing the road he drove out on.
Take this. It is not payment, I could not pay you for that. It is what I would have spent going out there myself, and I am too old to have got there.

note: THE THIRD CARAVAN
Dahab is coming home. Ummi Reyhan paid you out of her own pocket.

topics.label: Who runs this market?
replies: The broker thinks he does. The stalls think they do.
It is the camels. Everything in Kufa moves at the speed of something that has to drink.

topics.label: Later, Ummi.
replies: I am not going anywhere. Neither are they.

npcs.bio: Has kept the pen at the dead end of the lane for forty years. Sees every cart that goes west, because the west end of the lane is her end and there is no other way out of it.

npcs.name: Master Faruq

lines.text: What is this place?
A running track with the town’s water underneath it.

Kufa keeps its reserve down there — the cistern head is the ring in the middle of the infield. Every crew in the caravan trade stands a Watch on it. It is the oldest job in this town and until this season it was ceremonial.

topics.label: How do I play?
replies: Five from the spot. You take five and I keep, then I take five and you keep. Most goals wins, and it stops the moment it cannot be caught.
One button, three times. A marker sweeps the goalmouth — press to pick your corner. Then a bar fills and empties — press to strike.
When it is my turn the marker sweeps again, and you press to dive.
Hit it flat out and it goes over the bar. Side-foot it into a corner I have guessed and I keep it out. That is the whole game.

topics.label: Why are there monsters on the field?
replies: This is Kufa’s only grass, and they are drawn to it.
Grass grows here because of the water under the ground — so we made a soccer field on top of it, and a stadium round the field, to protect it.
More monsters than ever this season. But more water bandits too. So they help keep the bandits out, and I have stopped complaining about them.

topics.label: I can clear them out for you.
replies: Three waves is a Watch. Break three and the draw is yours and the town pays it.
Put the drain mouths down as well and I will pay you again out of the crews’ purse, because they will vote for it.

note: THE CISTERN WATCH
Break three waves at the cistern head. The gun on the head is up. The drain mouths are worth a second purse.

topics.label: Until this season?
replies: The drains run out to the west road. When the road wells are full, the drains are full, and nothing lives in a full drain.

The road wells are not full. So things are walking up the drains and out onto my infield, and they go for the cistern head every time — not for the crews, for the WATER. You cannot chase them. You have to stand between them and it.
Three waves is a Watch. Break three and the draw is yours and the town pays it. Put the drain mouths down as well and I will pay you again out of the crews’ purse, because they will vote for it.
And I will have the crews wind the old gun up out of the head for you. It is ceremonial. It has also been maintained every month for ninety years by foxes who did not believe it was ceremonial.

note: THE CISTERN WATCH
Break three waves at the cistern head. The gun on the head is up. The drain mouths are worth a second purse.

topics.label: Why does the town let anyone stand it?
replies: Because the roster is crews, and a crew is whoever a crew says it is.
You walked in off the road. Out here that is a qualification.

topics.label: Who else has stood it?
replies: Sura, four times, and she has never taken the purse.
Bahri once, before the oasis. Half the barracks. Not the broker, before you ask, and everybody has noticed.

topics.label: I will look around first.
replies: Mind the infield. It is the only grass in Kufa.

topics.label: What do you do here when there is no water to guard?
replies: This was a football ground before it was a cistern head, and it will be one again the day somebody remembers to cut the grass.
I kept goal for the works side for eleven years. Eleven. Nobody has put five past me in this ground and nobody is going to.
There is a ball in the equipment store and there is a spot painted on that grass, and you have just spent an afternoon clearing the only thing standing between them.

note: FIVE FROM THE SPOT
Faruq kept goal for the works side for eleven years. He would like you to know it.

topics.label: About that shootout.
replies: Eleven years, and the fox who broke the siphon comes out here and does that to me on my own line.
I have written it in the book. The crews will read it. I am not going to enjoy the next six weeks and neither are you, because they are going to want a game every time you come through that tunnel.

npcs.bio: Runs the Cistern Watch. Believes the stadium was built over the cistern head on purpose, so that the day it needed defending there would already be a crowd standing round it.

npcs.name: Dahab

lines.text: You are a long way out.
I work here. I am told I work here.
Do not stand still in the open. It does not care about you but it is very bad at going round things.

topics.label: Ummi Reyhan sent me.
replies: My aunt.
She would. She counts everything.

We drove out four months ago and the station was already theirs. They kept the carts, they kept the crews, and they have been running us out to the pipe head and back ever since — they need hands, and hands that nobody in town is looking for are the cheapest kind.
Tell her the cart is fine. She will ask about the cart.

note: DAHAB
Alive at the way station. Ummi Reyhan is at the camel pen in the bazaar.

topics.label: What is the rig doing?
replies: Drinking the road.
The pipe goes down further than any well in Kufa. It is not taking from the wells — it is taking from underneath them, and they are going dry in the order the pipe reaches them.
The one in the plated coat runs it. Put him down and it stops. I have watched them all week: nobody else out here knows how to start it again.

topics.label: Stay down. I will be back.
replies: I have got very good at that.

npcs.bio: Drove a cart west with the third caravan four months ago and has been at the way station ever since, hauling for the rig that took the road he drove out on.

npcs.name: Ghazi

lines.text: You are hiring.
I have been hiring for five weeks. That is not the same as finding anybody.
Three wagons, loaded, standing in the pen. Two legs of road. Nobody will walk in front of them.

topics.label: What is the job?
replies: Walk in front of my wagons from here to the way station on the far leg. Two legs. They roll when the road in front of them is clear and they stop when it is not, which is the whole of what you are being paid for.
They are slow and they are loud and everything on that road wants them more than it wants you. That is the good news, if you are any good.
Come back and say yes when you mean it.

note: CARAVAN — HIRING
Ghazi wants an escort from the bazaar to the way station. Two legs.

topics.label: Why has nobody taken it?
replies: Because the second leg is where the last two went.
Idris will tell you he lost two caravans. He lost two caravans I loaded.

topics.label: I will walk in front of them.
replies: Say that again outside so the pen hears it.
They are hitched. Go west out of the market and they will be on the road behind you before you reach the first milestone.
One thing. They do not wait for you and they do not run from anything. If it gets in among them, that is the end of it — there is no second set of wagons.
Then you are not walking it alone. There is a second name on the sheet — Kass, came to the pen this morning and asked for half what the last one wanted.
Two swords for three wagons of dry goods. I have stopped arguing with my own good luck.

note: THE CARAVAN IS ON THE ROAD
It rolls when the road ahead is clear and stops when it is not. West, through the bazaar mouth.

topics.label: It is done. All three, at the station.
replies: I have had the runner. He came the whole way at a walk, in daylight, on his own.
That is the part nobody is going to believe.
Take it, and take the standing offer with it: this board is yours whenever you want a road walked.

note: THE ROAD IS OPEN
Ghazi paid in full, and the board is yours whenever you want it.

topics.label: Not today.
replies: The wagons will keep. They have kept five weeks.

topics.label: What is on the board?
replies: Four wagons of empty cistern to the way station, and they come back full. That is the whole trade now — the pipe head runs again and nobody has moved a drop of it east.
Both legs. Same road you walked, and it is not the same road, because everything that watched the last one go through knows the wagons are worth stopping now.
Two hundred and sixty, and I do not haggle at my own board.

topics.label: — THE CISTERN TRAIN. I will take it.
replies: Then get in front of them.

note: THE CISTERN TRAIN
Four wagons to the way station and back. Both legs.

topics.label: The train job is done.
replies: Full cistern, both ends, no crew lost. Sign here.
You will notice the desert did not agree to any of this. It never does. It just gets walked through.

topics.label: Anything that is not walking in front of wagons?
replies: Idris has a repair crew who will not go out to the pipe head while there is anything standing between the milestone and the station, and I do not blame them — they carry spanners.
No wagons. No escort. Walk the far leg and clear it, all of it, and come back and tell me it is quiet.
A hundred and eighty. Less than the haulage, and you will be home before dark.

topics.label: — THE PIPE-HEAD SWEEP. I will take it.
replies: Far leg. Everything on it.

note: THE PIPE-HEAD SWEEP
Clear the far leg so Idris’s repair crew can work. No wagons.

topics.label: The sweep job is done.
replies: The crew went out this morning with a cart and a kettle and they have not sent anybody back at a run, which is how I know.
Take it.

topics.label: Something short. I have business in town.
replies: One leg. Bazaar mouth to the milestone, two wagons of grain for the station crews, and you can be back in the market for the evening.
It is the short one and it is not the safe one. Everything that used to spread itself over two legs is now sitting on one, because the far leg has a repair crew on it with a kettle.
Two hundred.

topics.label: — THE MILESTONE RUN. I will take it.
replies: One leg. Let us go.

note: THE MILESTONE RUN
Two wagons of grain to the milestone. First leg only.

topics.label: The run job is done.
replies: At the milestone by noon. The crews had the grain off before the wheels stopped.
You are becoming a thing that people at this end of the market plan around. I hope you know what you have done to yourself.

topics.label: I want the big one.
replies: Then here it is, and it is the one I have been waiting nine years to load.
Six wagons. Full. Going WEST. Water OUT of Kufa, along the road that spent four months carrying it the other way in the dark, in daylight, with the Emir’s seal on the manifest and my name under it.
Every well on that road is drinking again and the stations downline are not, and I am going to be the one who fixes that in front of witnesses.
Four hundred and twenty, and walk slowly. I want it seen.

topics.label: — THE WESTWARD TRAIN. I will take it.
replies: Load them. I will walk in front.

note: THE WESTWARD TRAIN
Six wagons of water going west. Both legs, in daylight.

topics.label: The train job is done.
replies: They are through. Nine wells, six wagons, and a road that people used to write hostile action, cause unknown at the bottom of.
That is the board finished with you, in the sense that there is nothing on it I can put in front of you that you have not already done twice.
Come back anyway. It refills.

topics.label: I am walking away from the contract.
replies: You are not the first and I will not write it down.
The board keeps. Come back when the road looks smaller.

topics.label: What is on the board?
replies: Empty, and I have never been able to say that before.
Give it a week. The road works now, so there will be more of it than there ever was.

topics.label: Who else is walking it?
replies: One. Kass. Came to the pen the morning I put the second name on the sheet, which I have decided not to think about.
He asked for half what the last one asked for and he has not asked me a single question since. Both of those should worry me and neither of them does.

topics.label: About the fox who walked it with me.
replies: He is not on my sheet twice, if that is what you are asking. One run. He asked for one run.
Whatever he was doing on my road, he did it standing in front of my wagons, so I am not going to be the one who says a word about it.

npcs.bio: Hires crews at the board. Has had the same three wagons loaded and standing in the pen for five weeks because nobody will walk in front of them.

npcs.name: Kass

lines.text: They put four hours of something into my arm and told me to lie still. I have been lying still for four days.

topics.label: How bad is it?
replies: Bad enough that I am glad of the table.
Not bad enough to be quiet.

topics.label: The 9th GATE.
replies: A gate is a road between two places that have never had one. Nine of them, and the ninth has been shut since before the Emir’s grandfather signed anything.
King Might is on the other side of it. That is not a rumour I heard in a bar, that is a line in a file I was carrying when they cut me.
You have the crystal. Do not sell it, do not show it, and do not tell me where you are taking it.

topics.label: What happens to this place now?
replies: Eleven of us down here. Four will come with me. Three will go to KASPER the moment the shaft opens and I know which three.
That is not a problem. That is a list.
Somebody has to stay on Kufa and keep it honest. It was always going to be whoever was left standing in this room.

topics.label: Nothing. Rest.
replies: That is the first sensible thing anyone has said to me all week.

npcs.bio: Up, and not steady, and not going to mention it.

npcs.name: Nasr

lines.text: You are standing in a room that does not exist. Try to look like you understand that.

topics.label: He is bleeding. Move.
replies: We are moving.
Ward is through that door and it has been ready for nine years for a day nobody wanted.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then get out of the way.

npcs.bio: Has run this station for nine years on a budget nobody will put in writing, and has stopped being able to tell the difference between keeping it open and keeping it.

npcs.name: Diya

lines.text: Nasr does the talking. I do the counting, and the counting is worse.

topics.label: You knew he was coming.
replies: We knew somebody was. Four days ago.
Take his legs or take the door. Either.

npcs.bio: Does the arithmetic for this station. Knows to the day how long it can go on without selling something.

npcs.name: Nasr

lines.text: He will keep. Which is more than I would have said an hour ago.

topics.label: Nine years down here.
replies: Nine years and four months.
You do not get told you are finished. You get told the allowance is under review, and then you get told it again.

topics.label: What is Station 9 for?
replies: Watching. That is the whole of it and it used to be enough.
We are the reason two caravans a year get through that KASPER would rather did not. Nobody will ever know that, which is the job.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then let him sleep.

npcs.bio: Has run this station for nine years on a budget nobody will put in writing, and has stopped being able to tell the difference between keeping it open and keeping it.

npcs.name: Diya

lines.text: He lost about a third of it on your road. I have seen worse walk out of here.

topics.label: How long can this place last?
replies: Fourteen months. That is not a guess, it is a column.
Nasr thinks I say that to frighten him. I say it because it is fourteen months.

npcs.bio: Does the arithmetic for this station. Knows to the day how long it can go on without selling something.

npcs.name: Rukaya

lines.text: You came up the road. On purpose.
Then you are either lost, hired, or the sort of trouble I would rather have inside the gate than out.

topics.label: The book. Who has come through?
replies: Everyone. That is the whole point of a book.
Eleven years. Four hundred and six wagons in, three hundred and ninety-one out. The fifteen are the reason anybody remembers my name.
Two caravans in one season, both on the far leg, both between the milestone and the choke. Ghazi lost the second one and has not put a train on that road since.
Everybody says bandits. Bandits take the wagons. Whatever took those two went past the wagons and I have never once been asked why I know that.

note: THE STATION BOOK
Four hundred and six in, three hundred and ninety-one out. Whatever took the missing fifteen went PAST the wagons.

topics.label: The rig on your forecourt.
replies: It came on eight carts with a permit I was not allowed to read.
It is not taking my water. It is taking what my water sits on, which is a distinction the permit was very careful about.

topics.label: The head is running again.
replies: It is. And the crews have gone back to sleeping through the night, which is the only measure of anything out here that I trust.
The station keeps a purse for whoever fixes what the station cannot. It has not been opened in eleven years. Take it before I think better of it.

topics.label: The guard who walked in cut.
replies: On his feet, and would not sit down, and would not give a name to the book.
I have written "one guard, unnamed, walked in" and I have written the date, and that is all anybody will ever get out of me about it.
Whatever he is, he stood in front of Ghazi’s wagons. That buys a blank line in my book and it buys it cheaply.

topics.label: The one in the plated coat.
replies: He stood in that gateway and he said it, and I wrote it, and my hand was not steady.
Eleven years of a book that only ever counted wagons, and the entry that will outlive me is four words and a name.
The berth is the station’s now. I have no idea what a station does with a berth and I intend to find out slowly.

topics.label: The field up the track is quiet now.
replies: It is. And nobody has told me why, and I have not asked.
I have written "the pad closed" and the date. That is the whole entry and it is the only one in eleven years that I know is a lie by omission.
I would rather have the road working than the name. Most days.

topics.label: Three, on foot, going west.
replies: You have read the line. There is nothing under it.
I will tell you what is not in the book, which is that they looked like people who had been told a time and were late for it.
And I have run a gate for eleven years, so I know exactly what that looks like, and I have never once been able to write it down.

topics.label: Nothing. Water and a wall is enough.
replies: It is more than the road offers. Rest as long as you like.

npcs.bio: Eleven years at the far end of the worst road on the planet. Keeps the book, the water and a very short list of people whose word she will take.

npcs.name: Bashir

lines.text: Careful of the boards. Half of this yard is pipe with a plank over it.

topics.label: What is your crew for?
replies: Opening the head, clearing the head and shutting the head. That is the whole trade and I am good at it.
We have not opened it in fourteen months. Every time we are ready, the draw drops and the Emir’s office says wait.
I am not saying anything about that. I am saying we are ready and we wait.

topics.label: The far leg is quiet now.
replies: I know. My carts came up it without an escort for the first time since I have been here.
You will not get thanked for that by anyone who matters. You are being thanked by someone who does not, which is worse and lasts longer.

topics.label: What did the rig actually do?
replies: It went under the head. Not into it — UNDER it, into the water the head stands in, which is water nobody has a permit for because nobody thought you could reach it.
Nine wells failed in order going east. That is not a drought. A drought does not queue.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Mind the boards.

npcs.bio: Eight foxes, forty metres of pipe and a head he has not been allowed to open. Very careful about whose name he says out loud.

npcs.name: Nuri

lines.text: You are not on the sheet. Nobody is ever on the sheet and I have stopped writing the sheet.

topics.label: What goes up that gantry?
replies: Water. Which is a thing I am told not to say, so I say "bulk".
Three carts a week for four months, west empty and back heavy, and every one of them weighed to the drop by me personally.
And the weight going UP has never once matched the weight coming IN. It is always more. I have raised it twice.
The second time, a fox in a plated coat came and stood exactly where you are standing and did not say anything at all, and I have not raised it since.

note: THE WEIGHBRIDGE
More goes up the gantry than ever comes in on the carts. It is not the wells being sold. It is what the wells sit on.

topics.label: Who is the one in the plated coat?
replies: No name. Not withheld — there has never been one to withhold.
Sheets come signed from the Emir’s office and countersigned with a mark that is not a name, and he stands on the ramp while they load, and then the ship goes.
I would know him anywhere and I could not tell you one true thing about him.

topics.label: Those beams across the top.
replies: Cutters. They part a container the way you would part a loaf.
They run whether anything is on the strip or not, which tells you what this place thinks a person is worth.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Right you are.

npcs.bio: Weighs what goes up the gantry and writes the number down. Has never once been told what any of it is, and has stopped finding that strange, which is the part that bothers him.

npcs.name: The Plated Coat

lines.text: You came up the track rather than the road. Everybody does, eventually.
The rig is off. I have known that for two days and I am still here, which should tell you something about how much the rig mattered.

topics.label: The rig on the pipe head was yours.
replies: The rig was leased, the permit was signed, the berth is paid for eleven years forward and every sheet in the chain has a real name on it. Not mine. That is the craft.
I did not take Kufa’s water. I bought a surplus that a man told me was a surplus, from an office entitled to sell it.
He was lying, and I knew, and knowing is not a crime anywhere I have ever worked.

topics.label: Nine wells failed in order, going east.
replies: Yes. That is what happens.

You have decided that the order is the evidence. It is not — the order is just physics. The evidence is that nobody in this town wrote the order down for four years, and that is not something I did to Kufa.
A place that will not look at its own numbers will always find somebody like me eventually. I am the weather.

topics.label: Somebody paid for the frames at the choke.
replies: I did. I paid over the odds and I would like you to know that, because the alternative is that you think I am careless.
A load moved under heavy guard is a load worth stopping. Somebody in Ghazi’s pen told somebody in a tavern and it reached me in a morning. That is not a conspiracy, it is a market.
The guard was not in the price. I am not going to pretend to be sorry about him, but he was not in the price.

note: WHO PAID FOR THE CHOKE
He did, and over the odds. Somebody in the pen told somebody in a tavern and it reached the berth in a morning.

topics.label: You want the crystal.
replies: I want it the way you want the road to work. Not greedily. Structurally.

Here is the offer and it is a real one, so hear all of it. Six thousand, the berth signed over to the way station, and the sheets — every sheet, four years of them, with the Emir’s signature on the top one.
You would walk down that track able to prove everything to everyone, and Kufa would have its water and its answer in the same afternoon.
And I would have a stone that is no use to anybody on this planet, and a berth I have finished with anyway.
You are already deciding no. I would like you to at least do me the courtesy of noticing that it was the better outcome for everybody standing on this rock.

note: THE OFFER
Six thousand, the berth, and four years of signed sheets, for the crystal. He is not wrong that it is the better afternoon for Kufa.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then stand there. I have four years of practice at it.

topics.label: No.
replies: No.
Then we are going to do the other thing, and I want to be clear that I have not enjoyed a single part of the last four years and I am going to enjoy this.

npcs.bio: Buys what is not for sale by finding the person for whom it has become the least bad option. Has been on Kufa four years and has never given anybody a name to put in a book.

npcs.name: Kass

lines.text: You came back down. I did not think you would.
Sit if you want. Nobody here has worked out what the chairs are for yet.

topics.label: You said four. Who are they?
replies: Sahar on the comms, Tal in stores, Ammar who put me back together, and Diya, who is not here yet and will be.

Not one of them is here because of a speech. Sahar because somebody she trusted walked out. Tal because he has been sitting on an arithmetic problem for nine years. Ammar because he kept a table serviced for a day nobody wanted and then got the day.
That is what a thing like this is actually made of. Four separate old grievances that happen to point the same way for a month.

topics.label: Nasr said three would run.
replies: He did. He said four would come with him and three would go to KASPER, and he counted eleven and he did not count me.
He was right about the three. They went up the shaft the night the arch opened and they took the station’s own bearings with them.
I need to know where they went before somebody buys them, and I cannot send anybody up that shaft who has ever been seen in this station.
You can go anywhere on this planet and nobody thinks twice. Ask at the way station. Whatever went west, she will have written it down.

note: THE THREE
Three of the eleven went up the shaft the night the arch opened. Ask Rukaya at the way station — she writes down everything that goes west.

topics.label: Rukaya has them in the book.
replies: Say it.

topics.label: The fox at the dock.
replies: Bahri. Nine years sitting in a boat on a pond with no fish in it, and in nine years nobody walked down that jetty who should not have.
Everybody down here calls him the doorman. Nobody has ever once asked him what he thinks about any of it, including me, including tonight.
Go and ask him. Not for me — I want to know what he says when it is not an order.

topics.label: What were you, before the wagons?
replies: Ghazi asked me that. I said dry goods and he let me have it.
Nine years in this station. I have walked into four rooms on this planet and told four different lies about why, and every one of them worked, which is the part I would like you to sit with.
The one true thing I have said out loud since the choke was no. I am going to try to build the rest of it out of that.

topics.label: The crystal.
replies: It is not mine and it was never going to be. I could have carried it up the shaft and it would have been in a lockup in a fortnight.
You are going to walk it off this planet and I am going to spend a long time not knowing whether that was right.
When you find the 9th GATE, you will not need to send word. I will hear about it. Everybody will.

topics.label: The one in the plated coat.
replies: I know. Sahar had it off the freight band before you were down the shaft.
Four years he stood on that pad and the whole planet had a phrase for him instead of a name. That is not him being clever. That is us.
And it is the argument I lost in the ward, in one sentence, which Nasr has not mentioned and will not.

topics.label: Nasr is still upstairs.
replies: He runs the station. He will go on running it, and I am not going to try to take it off him, because the day I do this stops being about the crystal and starts being about me.
He was right about the money. That is the thing nobody in this room wants to hear me say and I am going to keep saying it.
If we are only right because he is a villain then we are not right.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then sit a while. It is warm in here.

npcs.bio: On his feet, cut across the face and down one arm, and running a meeting for the first time in his life. Nobody has voted on this and nobody is going to.

npcs.name: Sahar

lines.text: I have the freight band, the Emir’s office and four of the wells. Ask me anything and give me ten minutes.

topics.label: Why did you say yes?
replies: Zubair taught me this desk. Everything I know about listening to a planet, he sat behind me and taught me.
And he went up that shaft with the station’s bearings in his coat, and he did not say goodbye, and I would have covered for him if he had.
So I am not doing this because I am brave. I am doing it because I would like to find out whether he was ever telling me the truth about anything.

topics.label: What can you actually hear?
replies: The freight band, which is how I knew about the pad. The Emir’s office, which is dull and honest now and was neither. Four wellheads.
And Station 9’s own traffic, which is the one nobody thinks to encrypt because who would be listening.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: I will be here.

npcs.bio: Twenty-one, and has been listening to this planet for three years with better ears than anybody has ever given her credit for.

npcs.name: Tal

lines.text: Everything in this wing is signed out to a project that was cancelled in the first year. Including the lamps.

topics.label: Why did you say yes?
replies: Because this station is paid by two people and has been since the second year, and I am the only one who ever sees both sets of paper.
I raised it once. I was told it was a clerical overlap and that the second account was a contingency, and I wrote that down too, with the date.
Nine years I have had a ledger that says we were bought, and nine years nobody asked me a question I could answer honestly. Kass asked one on his second day out of the ward.

note: TWO SETS OF PAPER
Station 9 has been paid by two accounts since its second year. Tal has the ledger, with dates.

topics.label: What did the three take?
replies: Bearings, two long-range sets, and eleven days of water for three foxes, which is not eleven days of water for three foxes going anywhere sensible.
They signed for none of it. That is how I knew before anybody told me.
West on foot with that load means they were meeting something. Nobody walks west out of here for the scenery.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Right.

npcs.bio: Signs for everything that comes down the shaft and has signed for nine years of a number that does not work.

npcs.name: Ammar

lines.text: He should be lying down. He knows he should be lying down. We have had that conversation and I lost it.

topics.label: Why did you say yes?
replies: I have kept that table serviced for nine years. Sterile, stocked, lamp tested every month, for a day nobody in this station wanted to come.
Everybody thought it was superstition. It was the only part of my job I was allowed to do properly.
Then somebody walked down four hundred metres of mined corridor with a third of himself missing and lay down on it. And two hours later Nasr told me to take a thing off him.
I have spent nine years getting a room ready for one fox. I was not going to spend the same evening helping rob him.

topics.label: Will he be all right?
replies: He will have that face for the rest of his life and the arm will be about eighty per cent.
Physically he is the easiest patient I have ever had. He does exactly what you tell him and none of it works, because he then gets up.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Go careful.

npcs.bio: Serviced a table under a lamp for nine years for a day nobody wanted, and got the day, and has not sat down since.

npcs.name: Diya

lines.text: I put you on the floor of that ward and you put me on it. We are not going to talk about that.

topics.label: You drew on me.
replies: I did, and I would like to tell you I have thought better of the reasoning and I have not. It was never his to hold. He was carrying it.
What I have thought better of is the sentence after that one.
Because Nasr said take it off him, and I moved, and I did not ask a single question first. Nine years of training to ask questions.

topics.label: Why come over now?
replies: Nasr counted eleven of us and he got four and three and himself, and he told me the numbers a week before any of it happened.
He had me in the four. Kass had me in his four as well, and Kass has been in this station nine years pretending to be somewhere else.
Two men counted the same room. One of them counted himself into it and one of them counted himself out. That is the entire difference and it took me four days to see it.

note: THE ARITHMETIC
Nasr counted eleven and made four, three and himself. Kass counted eleven and made four. Only one of them left himself out of the sum.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Fine.

npcs.bio: Drew on you in the ward, lost, and spent the four days afterwards reading a charter nobody has opened since the founding.

npcs.name: Nasr

lines.text: You are welcome down here, which surprises me as much as it does you.
Four of my people are sitting in a store room I signed off nine years ago, and I have not shut the door on them, and I would like some credit for that which I am not going to get.

topics.label: You tried to take it off him.
replies: I did. And if you come back in ten years and this station is a hole full of water because nobody would sell anything, come and tell me I was wrong.
I am not the villain of your evening. I am the man who has kept eleven people alive under a pond on a budget that was cut twice.
What I got wrong was the doorway. He stood in it and said no and I had never once considered that anybody down here would.

topics.label: Three of yours ran.
replies: I said which three a week before they went. Nobody wrote it down, which is the closest thing to a confession you will get out of me.
I could have stopped them. I did not, because a station that has to lock its own people in is finished anyway.
Tell Kass that. He will not like where it leads.

topics.label: Nothing.
replies: Then good evening.

npcs.bio: Still runs the station. Has not apologised, has not been asked to, and is still right about the money.

npcs.name: The Plated Coat

lines.text: You were going to walk onto that pad and leave.

topics.label: How did you know?
replies: A thing that size does not move across a planet quietly.
Four people told me for nothing. One of them thought he was complaining about the weather.

topics.label: You are standing on a crest.
replies: I am standing on a landing pad that a crest was painted round. I would rather you noticed the difference before we start.

npcs.bio: Buys what is not for sale by finding the person for whom it has become the least bad option. Has been on Kufa four years and has never given anybody a name to put in a book.

npcs.name: Coat Guard

lines.text: Keep walking. He is the one you want.

npcs.bio: Plate, and nothing out here is made of plate.

npcs.name: Coat Guard

npcs.bio: Plate, and nothing out here is made of plate.
